files.finding: Resource validation assigns nil when the pointer is set but the daemon reports OomKillDisable unsupported; only a true requested value generates the discard warning. The memory resource constructor forwards a nonnil pointer to OCI and otherwise omits it.
ContainerStart revalidates the existing HostConfig against current system settings before starting the container.
The info response exposes cgroup version and the sysinfo OomKillDisable capability; the source separately notes that the feature is unavailable on cgroup v2.
The container resource type represents OomKillDisable as an optional boolean pointer, allowing distinct null and false serialization.

official_primary_sources.interpretation: The observed false-to-null change is consistent with source-defined removal of an unsupported option during start revalidation. This establishes a bounded compatibility rationale, not a claim that arbitrary null-valued HostConfig changes are safe.

allowed_transition.reverse_null_to_false: Reject as an unexplained lifecycle mutation; it is not needed by the observed source-defined start transition.

comparison_design: Keep exact full raw inspect records and their hashes. Produce a separate typed comparison view and an explicit transformation record containing policy ID/digest, field path, raw before/after, lifecycle phase and runtime-capability digest.
Validate the sandbox and reject enabled/malformed OomKillDisable before any canonical comparison. Deep-copy the view; never mutate retained raw data.

For an authorized created-to-started false-to-null pair only, substitute false in the comparison view for that single field and compare the entire remaining original identity/configuration with deterministic JSON bytes, preserving type distinctions and every unlisted key.

Reject every other changed HostConfig field, added/missing field, mount, image, argv, source label, namespace, memory/swap/CPU/PID/fd limit, security option, or ownership identifier. Do not drop HostConfig or compare only the currently hand-picked sandbox restrictions.

Keep candidate expected-created versus immediately-before-start comparison raw-exact. Apply the narrow transition rule only when comparing the original created identity to the final independently authenticated exited identity.

Apply the same rule to keeper created versus first-running comparison. Thereafter retain and compare the complete raw first-running keeper identity exactly on every before/after boundary; no mid-history null/false normalization.

State.OOMKilled, exit agreement, start/finish timestamps, restart count, conservative EOF confirmation, stream framing, cleanup, source staging, volume ownership and no-redispatch barriers are untouched.

raw_field_policy.reason: Disabling the OOM killer is never authorized; use strict type/identity checks, not Python equality that equates false with zero.

runtime_gate.other_identities: Keep existing daemon/socket/image/kernel/architecture binding. Freeze and recheck these capability fields with the stable runtime identity; a changed or unavailable capability cannot authorize normalization.

proposed_compatibility_contract.scope: Exactly HostConfig.OomKillDisable during the declared created-to-started lifecycle transition of the same fresh owned container.

preserve: All frozen v1 modules, helpers, tests, freeze snapshots and failed outputs remain byte-identical.
Keep the v1 57-case definitions, ordered recipes, expectations, controls and candidate bytes unchanged; reuse definitions as read-only input where imports permit.
A new source-domain execution identifier may change because the transport protocol changes; do not describe this as a candidate behavior change.
New outputs, prospective freeze, source hashes, runtime capability identity and policy digest are required. No overwrite, no automatic retry and no old observation reuse for acceptance.
recommended_versioning.why_observer_version: The frozen observer v1 accepts only binding protocol candidate-client-execution-v1. A v2 binding adapter/observer must explicitly accept the new controller contract while preserving all existing product assertions and unsupported dispositions; never relabel a v2 execution as v1.

required_regressions: Pure strict-type matrix: false->null accepted only in the named phase/profile; false->false and null->null accepted; true on either side, missing, numeric zero, strings, collections and reverse transition rejected.

Full identity sensitivity: retain the allowed false->null transition while mutating each relevant sandbox field, an otherwise-unlisted HostConfig field, field presence, container ID, source/fixture label, mount, argv or image; every independent mutation must still fail.
The comparison helper must preserve input object and raw byte identities; the transformation census must contain exactly the one allowed field and bind before/after/config/runtime/policy hashes.

Keeper lifecycle: initial false->running null accepted; running null->false or changed StartedAt/restart count/source mount denied; keeper/volume cleanup and continuous volume authority remain required.

Candidate lifecycle: created false remains raw-exact at pre-start; final null can match only alongside known natural wait/inspect agreement; OOM, kill, startup failure, timeout and capture uncertainty remain unqualified under existing rules.

Runtime binding: omit or change cgroup/capability/version/git/image/socket information, or report capability true; no compatibility exception. Retain complete runtime response evidence without using transient container counters in identity.
Observer v2 binding rejects v1 or substituted protocol/purpose/source/config while unchanged semantic assertions, unsupported-wrapper dispositions and known-exit preservation remain identical.

Root runs combined syntax/types/lint plus all affected offline classes after source review/freeze, then one new complete physical control and independent-process persistence qualification under the revised contract. If it fails, retain the result and diagnose before proposing another version.

Only after required controls qualify does root proceed to the prospectively registered remaining CLI histories; the failed v1 run supplies no passing candidate observations or statistical sample evidence.
risks_and_limits: Null does not universally mean false for Docker configuration. This exception is limited to one field, one typed transition and a runtime profile supported by inspected primary source.
A general recursive null/false normalizer would conceal real configuration changes and is explicitly excluded.

Runtime API response fields describe daemon capabilities and configuration; they do not independently prove kernel cgroup enforcement. Existing physical restrictions and qualification obligations remain.
Candidate created-to-exited normalization is prospective: no candidate reached start in the retained failed histories. It needs a new physical control, not extrapolated passing evidence.
Later daemon/API versions or lifecycle representation changes require separate evidence and a new prospective policy revision; do not widen the exception reactively during a frozen run.
No quality, ranking, timing advantage or statistical support for swarm versus orchestrator follows from this compatibility design.

runtime_evidence.limitation: Freeze-3 retained raw capability evidence supports this diagnosis. The v1 per-process runtime identity omits these capability fields, so the new contract must prospectively bind them before using compatibility normalization.
